newsitem.title: INDIA: India government agrees 29 pct tax shift to states.
newsitem.headline: India government agrees 29 pct tax shift to states.

text.p: Representatives of India's federal and state governments agreed on Tuesday that 29 percent of federal tax revenues would be transferred to the 26 states.

The decision, which must be approved by the states and parliament, would involve a total additional transfer of 50 billion rupees ($ 1.4 billion) to the states for the two years 1996/97 and 1997/98, Home Minister Indrajit Gupta said.
Gupta said the agreement was reached at a meeting of the steering committee of the Interstate Council, which represents states and is chaired by the home minister.

"Twenty-nine percent of total collection of taxes will go to the states," Gupta told reporters after a day-long meeting of the committee. He said it was proposed that the percentage would take effect retroactively as of April 1, 1996.
The proposal would have to be approved by the full Interstate Council and then by parliament before it could take effect.

Currently 77.5 percent of federal income tax revenues and and 47.5 percent of excise revenues are transferred to states. It was agreed that these would be combined with other tax categories to make a larger pool, 29 percent of which would go to the states.
Gupta said that if the 29 percent share were adopted, it would require the federal government to shift an additional 20 billion rupees to states for 1996/97 and 30 billion for 1997/98.
The states had pressed for a 33 percent share but finally agreed to 29 percent, he said.
"The consensus that emerged was to accept 29 percent and then review it in December and January," Gupta said.
